Maia for Project management

Turn project activity into the next decision.

Maia prepares updates from project records and the Slack conversations that explain them. Program and project managers can focus on dependencies, owners, and decisions that need attention.

All teams ↗

Report what changed

Project managers spend too much of a review rebuilding status that already exists. Maia can combine selected project records and channel decisions into an update focused on changed milestones, new risks, blocked dependencies, and decisions due.

Define the reporting period and which source owns dates, status, and scope. A concise update gives stakeholders a common view while leaving project judgment with the program manager.

Make dependencies concrete

A useful dependency names the delivering team, receiving team, expected artifact, required date, and impact of delay. Maia can extract those details from plans and discussion, then flag dependencies that lack an owner or confirmed date.

The teams validate the commitment. Maia should not infer agreement from a casual mention or assign a date because the plan needs one. The handoff becomes actionable when both sides can inspect and correct it in the thread.

Prepare stakeholder updates

Provide the approved plan, current status, recent decisions, and the audience's reporting template. Maia can draft a short update covering completed work, upcoming milestones, risks, decisions, and asks.

Internal and external audiences may require different detail. The project manager edits the narrative and verifies every commitment before sharing it. Source links let stakeholders drill into the record when they have access.

Capture meeting actions

After a project meeting, Maia can turn notes or a Slack discussion into decisions, owners, due dates, and unresolved questions. It can compare those actions with the current project record and propose updates.

The meeting owner confirms the recap. Any task creation or date change should show the exact destination and value first, so the system of record stays aligned with the decision people actually made.

Build a recurring program review

Schedule the same update after the team agrees on its sources and thresholds. Ask Maia to omit unchanged work and carry forward only overdue decisions or active dependencies. This makes the next review a continuation of the last one.

Corrections in the channel can refine reusable guidance, such as which status field takes precedence or when a dependency counts as at risk.

Start with one cross-team handoff

Choose a dependency that spans two teams and includes one missing owner or conflicting date. Check that Maia preserves the gap, links both sources, and asks the program manager for a decision. Then add the wider project portfolio.

The program manager can use the thread to close the loop. When an owner accepts a dependency or a date changes, Maia can draft the corresponding recap and proposed record update. Stakeholders see the decision in context, while the project system keeps the agreed plan.

Questions from project teams

Which project systems can Maia use?

That depends on your connected apps. An authorized export can support the first update while you validate live access.

Can Maia create and update tasks?

When those actions are supported, Maia can propose exact records for approval. Project owners still confirm scope, owner, and date.

How does Maia handle conflicting dates?

It should show both sources and their timestamps. The project manager applies the team's source-of-truth rule and resolves the conflict.
